title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
before: Comparing two sentences with BERT meant running the pair through the model together.
problem: Finding the closest match in a corpus required a forward pass per candidate, which is hopeless at scale.
breakthrough: Train BERT in a siamese setup so each sentence maps to a fixed vector that can be compared with cosine similarity.
why: It turned BERT into an embedding model, which is what makes semantic search and RAG practical.
next: DPR for retrieval, and the sentence-transformers ecosystem most RAG stacks still use.
inherits: The embedding model as a separate component from the generator.
